import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

@[simp] lemma of_eq_of {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) = ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 := Quotient.eq

instance : LE (Logic S) :=
  ⟨Quotient.lift₂ (· ≤ₛ ·) (fun 𝓢₁ 𝓣₁ 𝓢₂ 𝓣₂ h𝓢 h𝓣 ↦ by simp [WeakerThan, equiv_def.mp h𝓢, equiv_def.mp h𝓣])⟩

@[simp] lemma le_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ≤ ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

instance : PartialOrder (Logic S) where
  le_refl := fun Λ ↦ by induction Λ using Quotient.ind; simp
  le_trans := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ Λ₃ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₃ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact WeakerThan.trans
  le_antisymm := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact le_antisymm

@[simp] lemma lt_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) < ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

end Logic

@[simp] lemma provableSet_theory (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ⊢!* theory 𝓢 := fun hf ↦ hf

def Inconsistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop := ∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f

class Consistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop where
  not_inconsistent : ¬Inconsistent 𝓢

lemma inconsistent_def {𝓢 : S} :
    Inconsistent 𝓢 ↔ ∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f := by exact?

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

@[simp] lemma of_eq_of {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) = ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 := Quotient.eq

instance : LE (Logic S) :=
  ⟨Quotient.lift₂ (· ≤ₛ ·) (fun 𝓢₁ 𝓣₁ 𝓢₂ 𝓣₂ h𝓢 h𝓣 ↦ by simp [WeakerThan, equiv_def.mp h𝓢, equiv_def.mp h𝓣])⟩

@[simp] lemma le_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ≤ ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

instance : PartialOrder (Logic S) where
  le_refl := fun Λ ↦ by induction Λ using Quotient.ind; simp
  le_trans := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ Λ₃ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₃ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact WeakerThan.trans
  le_antisymm := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact le_antisymm

@[simp] lemma lt_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) < ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

end Logic

@[simp] lemma provableSet_theory (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ⊢!* theory 𝓢 := fun hf ↦ hf

def Inconsistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop := ∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f

class Consistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop where
  not_inconsistent : ¬Inconsistent 𝓢

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

@[simp] lemma of_eq_of {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) = ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 := Quotient.eq

instance : LE (Logic S) :=
  ⟨Quotient.lift₂ (· ≤ₛ ·) (fun 𝓢₁ 𝓣₁ 𝓢₂ 𝓣₂ h𝓢 h𝓣 ↦ by simp [WeakerThan, equiv_def.mp h𝓢, equiv_def.mp h𝓣])⟩

@[simp] lemma le_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ≤ ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

instance : PartialOrder (Logic S) where
  le_refl := fun Λ ↦ by induction Λ using Quotient.ind; simp
  le_trans := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ Λ₃ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₃ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact WeakerThan.trans
  le_antisymm := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact le_antisymm

@[simp] lemma lt_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) < ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

end Logic

@[simp] lemma provableSet_theory (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ⊢!* theory 𝓢 := fun hf ↦ hf

def Inconsistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop := ∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f

class Consistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop where
  not_inconsistent : ¬Inconsistent 𝓢

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

@[simp] lemma of_eq_of {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) = ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 := Quotient.eq

instance : LE (Logic S) :=
  ⟨Quotient.lift₂ (· ≤ₛ ·) (fun 𝓢₁ 𝓣₁ 𝓢₂ 𝓣₂ h𝓢 h𝓣 ↦ by simp [WeakerThan, equiv_def.mp h𝓢, equiv_def.mp h𝓣])⟩

@[simp] lemma le_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ≤ ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

instance : PartialOrder (Logic S) where
  le_refl := fun Λ ↦ by induction Λ using Quotient.ind; simp
  le_trans := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ Λ₃ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₃ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact WeakerThan.trans
  le_antisymm := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact le_antisymm

@[simp] lemma lt_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) < ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

end Logic

@[simp] lemma provableSet_theory (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ⊢!* theory 𝓢 := fun hf ↦ hf

def Inconsistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop := ∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f

class Consistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop where
  not_inconsistent : ¬Inconsistent 𝓢

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

@[simp] lemma of_eq_of {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) = ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 := Quotient.eq

instance : LE (Logic S) :=
  ⟨Quotient.lift₂ (· ≤ₛ ·) (fun 𝓢₁ 𝓣₁ 𝓢₂ 𝓣₂ h𝓢 h𝓣 ↦ by simp [WeakerThan, equiv_def.mp h𝓢, equiv_def.mp h𝓣])⟩

@[simp] lemma le_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ≤ ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

instance : PartialOrder (Logic S) where
  le_refl := fun Λ ↦ by induction Λ using Quotient.ind; simp
  le_trans := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ Λ₃ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₃ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact WeakerThan.trans
  le_antisymm := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact le_antisymm

@[simp] lemma lt_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) < ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

end Logic

@[simp] lemma provableSet_theory (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ⊢!* theory 𝓢 := fun hf ↦ hf

def Inconsistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop := ∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f

class Consistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop where
  not_inconsistent : ¬Inconsistent 𝓢

informal_statement: If you have a function `f` and you apply it to some value `phi`, then apply the inverse-like operation `f.l` to the result, you will get back to your original value `phi`.
informal_proof:
To see why this is true, consider the process step by step:
1. Let `phi` be any value.
2. Apply the function `f` to `phi`, resulting in `f.r phi`.
3. Then, apply `f.l` to `f.r phi`, which by definition undoes the application of `f`.
4. Therefore, `f.l (f.r phi)` must be equal to `phi`.

This shows that applying `f.r` followed by `f.l` returns you to your original value, effectively serving as an inverse operation.

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

@[simp] lemma of_eq_of {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) = ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 := Quotient.eq

instance : LE (Logic S) :=
  ⟨Quotient.lift₂ (· ≤ₛ ·) (fun 𝓢₁ 𝓣₁ 𝓢₂ 𝓣₂ h𝓢 h𝓣 ↦ by simp [WeakerThan, equiv_def.mp h𝓢, equiv_def.mp h𝓣])⟩

@[simp] lemma le_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ≤ ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

instance : PartialOrder (Logic S) where
  le_refl := fun Λ ↦ by induction Λ using Quotient.ind; simp
  le_trans := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ Λ₃ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₃ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact WeakerThan.trans
  le_antisymm := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact le_antisymm

@[simp] lemma lt_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) < ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

end Logic

@[simp] lemma provableSet_theory (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ⊢!* theory 𝓢 := fun hf ↦ hf

def Inconsistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop := ∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f

class Consistent (𝓢 : S) : Prop where
  not_inconsistent : ¬Inconsistent 𝓢

informal_statement: Applying a firewall `f.r` to a message that has been encrypted using a firewall `f.l` does not alter the original message.
informal_proof:
To prove that the composition of firewalls `f.r` and `f.l` does not alter the original message, we proceed as follows:

1. **Definition of Firewall Composition**: By definition, the composition of two firewalls `f.r` and `f.l` is represented by the application `f.r (f.l φ)`, where `φ` is the original message.

2. **Inverse Properties of Firewalls**: Assuming that `f.l` is an encryption firewall and `f.r` is a decryption firewall, they are designed as inverse functions. This means that decrypting an encrypted message retrieved by `f.l` should yield the original Message before encryption.

3. **Application of Simplification Lemma**: Using the `simp` tactic, which simplifies expressions based on known lemmas and definitions, we apply the `r_l_app` lemma. This lemma states that `f.r (f.l φ)` simplifies to `φ` directly, indicating that the composition of `f.r` and `f.l` preserves the original message `φ`.

4. **Conclusion**: Therefore, applying the firewall `f.r` to the message produced by `f.l φ` results in the original message `φ` unchanged, as required.

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

@[simp] lemma of_eq_of {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) = ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 := Quotient.eq

instance : LE (Logic S) :=

instance : PartialOrder (Logic S) where
  le_refl := fun Λ ↦ by induction Λ using Quotient.ind; simp
  le_trans := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ Λ₃ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₃ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact WeakerThan.trans
  le_antisymm := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact le_antisymm

@[simp] lemma lt_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) < ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

end Logic

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

@[simp] lemma of_eq_of {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) = ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 := Quotient.eq

instance : LE (Logic S) :=
  ⟨Quotient.lift₂ (· ≤ₛ ·) (fun 𝓢₁ 𝓣₁ 𝓢₂ 𝓣₂ h𝓢 h𝓣 ↦ by simp [WeakerThan, equiv_def.mp h𝓢, equiv_def.mp h𝓣])⟩

@[simp] lemma le_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ≤ ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

instance : PartialOrder (Logic S) where
  le_refl := fun Λ ↦ by induction Λ using Quotient.ind; simp
  le_trans := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ Λ₃ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₃ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact WeakerThan.trans
  le_antisymm := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact le_antisymm

@[simp] lemma lt_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) < ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 := by exact?

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

@[simp] lemma of_eq_of {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) = ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 := Quotient.eq

instance : LE (Logic S) :=
  ⟨Quotient.lift₂ (· ≤ₛ ·) (fun 𝓢₁ 𝓣₁ 𝓢₂ 𝓣₂ h𝓢 h𝓣 ↦ by simp [WeakerThan, equiv_def.mp h𝓢, equiv_def.mp h𝓣])⟩

@[simp] lemma le_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ≤ ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

instance : PartialOrder (Logic S) where
  le_refl := fun Λ ↦ by induction Λ using Quotient.ind; simp
  le_trans := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ Λ₃ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₃ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact WeakerThan.trans
  le_antisymm := fun Λ₁ Λ₂ ↦ by
    induction Λ₁ using Quotient.ind
    induction Λ₂ using Quotient.ind
    simp; exact le_antisymm

@[simp] lemma lt_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) < ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl
annotation: @[simp] lemma lt_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) < ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

namespace LO.System.Logic

variable {F : Type*} {S : Type*} {T : Type*} {U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]
informal_statement: If two functions ψ and φ are both injective or both surjective, then their composition φ∘ψ inherits that property. However, if one function is injective and the other is not surjective (or vice versa), the composition φ∘ψ only inherits the property of the latter function.
informal_proof:
First, assume that both ψ and φ are injective. To prove that φ∘ψ is injective, suppose that φ∘ψ(x) = φ∘ψ(y). Then φ(ψ(x)) = φ(ψ(y)). Since φ is injective, this implies ψ(x) = ψ(y). Because ψ is injective, ψ(x) = ψ(y) implies x = y. Thus, φ∘ψ is injective.

Next, assume that both ψ and φ are surjective. To prove that φ∘ψ is surjective, let z be an arbitrary element of the codomain of φ∘ψ. Since φ is surjective, there exists some y in the domain of φ such that φ(y) = z. Since ψ is surjective, there exists some x in the domain of ψ such that ψ(x) = y. Therefore, φ∘ψ(x) = φ(y) = z. Thus, φ∘ψ is surjective.

If one function is injective and the other is not necessarily injective or surjective, the composition inherits the property of the latter function. For example, if ψ is injective and φ is not injective, then φ∘ψ is not necessarily injective because φ might not preserve the distinctness introduced by ψ. Similarly, if ψ is not surjective and φ is surjective, then φ∘ψ is not necessarily surjective because the lack of surjectivity in ψ could result in elements not being mapped to by φ∘ψ. 

Thus, the composition φ∘ψ inherits injectivity only if both ψ and φ are injective, and it inherits surjectivity only if both ψ and φ are surjective. If only one function possesses the property, the composition inherits it from the latter function.

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

@[simp] lemma of_eq_of {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) = ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 := Quotient.eq

instance : LE (Logic S) :=
  ⟨Quotient.lift₂ (· ≤ₛ ·) (fun 𝓢₁ 𝓣₁ 𝓢₂ 𝓣₂ h𝓢 h𝓣 ↦ by simp [WeakerThan, equiv_def.mp h𝓢, equiv_def.mp h𝓣])⟩

@[simp] lemma le_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ≤ ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

instance : PartialOrder (Logic S) where
  le_refl := fun Λ ↦ by exact?

informal_statement: For any function \( f \), composing it with the identity function \( \text{Translation.id} \) on the left leaves \( f \) unchanged. In other words, \( \text{Translation.id} \) serves as the left identity in the composition of functions.
informal_proof:
The identity function \( \text{Translation.id} \) is defined to return its input unchanged; that is, for any input \( x \), \( \text{Translation.id}(x) = x \). When composing \( \text{Translation.id} \) with an arbitrary function \( f \), the output of \( f \) is passed directly to \( \text{Translation.id} \), resulting in \( \text{Translation.id}(f(x)) = f(x) \) for all \( x \). 

Since this equality holds for all \( f \) and all \( x \), it follows by the definition of function composition that \( \text{Translation.id} \circ f = f \). The proof is thus complete by the very nature of the identity function's definition within the framework of function composition.

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

@[simp] lemma of_eq_of {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) = ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 := Quotient.eq

instance : LE (Logic S) :=
  ⟨Quotient.lift₂ (· ≤ₛ ·) (fun 𝓢₁ 𝓣₁ 𝓢₂ 𝓣₂ h𝓢 h𝓣 ↦ by simp [WeakerThan, equiv_def.mp h𝓢, equiv_def.mp h𝓣])⟩

@[simp] lemma le_iff {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) ≤ ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by exact?

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := iff_of_eq rfl

namespace Logic

@[simp] lemma of_eq_of {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : (⟦𝓢⟧ : Logic S) = ⟦𝓣⟧ ↔ 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 := Quotient.eq

instance : LE (Logic S) :=
  ⟨Quotient.lift₂ (· ≤ₛ ·) (fun 𝓢₁ 𝓣₁ 𝓢₂ 𝓣₂ h𝓢 h𝓣 ↦ by exact?

is equivalent to the type of maps `α₂ → β₂`. -/
-- Porting note: removing `congr` attribute
@[simps apply]
def arrowCongr {α₁ β₁ α₂ β₂ : Sort*} (e₁ : α₁ ≃ α₂) (e₂ : β₁ ≃ β₂) : (α₁ → β₁) ≃ (α₂ → β₂) where
  toFun f := e₂ ∘ f ∘ e₁.symm
  invFun f := e₂.symm ∘ f ∘ e₁
  left_inv f := funext fun x => by simp only [comp_apply, symm_apply_apply]
  right_inv f := funext fun x => by simp only [comp_apply, apply_symm_apply]

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

informal_statement: The principle of extensionality states that two types are equal if they behave the same way in all contexts.
informal_proof: To prove the principle of extensionality, we start by considering two types \( A \) and \( B \). If \( A \) and \( B \) are such that they have the same elements when viewed from any context, this means that for any property or function, \( A \) and \( B \) behave identically.
