import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := Quotient (equiv S)

variable {S}

lemma equiv_def {𝓢 𝓣 : S} : 𝓢 ≈ 𝓣 ↔ theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣 := by exact?

C1_dependencies.name: rfl
C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

rag.content:
/-- If `α₁` is equivalent to `α₂` and `β₁` is equivalent to `β₂`, then the type of maps `α₁ → β₁`
is equivalent to the type of maps `α₂ → β₂`. -/
-- Porting note: removing `congr` attribute
@[simps apply]
def arrowCongr {α₁ β₁ α₂ β₂ : Sort*} (e₁ : α₁ ≃ α₂) (e₂ : β₁ ≃ β₂) : (α₁ → β₁) ≃ (α₂ → β₂) where
  toFun f := e₂ ∘ f ∘ e₁.symm
  invFun f := e₂.symm ∘ f ∘ e₁
  left_inv f := funext fun x => by simp only [comp_apply, symm_apply_apply]
  right_inv f := funext fun x => by simp only [comp_apply, apply_symm_apply]

/-- Composition of equivalences `e₁ : α ≃ β` and `e₂ : β ≃ γ`. -/
@[trans]
protected def trans (e₁ : α ≃ β) (e₂ : β ≃ γ) : α ≃ γ :=
  ⟨e₂ ∘ e₁, e₁.symm ∘ e₂.symm, e₂.left_inv.comp e₁.left_inv, e₂.right_inv.comp e₁.right_inv⟩

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := (· =ₛ ·)
  iseqv := { refl := fun _ ↦ rfl, symm := Eq.symm, trans := Eq.trans }

abbrev Logic := by exact?

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by simp [Equiv, WeakerThan]; intro e; rw [e]

end

variable (S)

instance equiv : Setoid S where
  r := by exact?

/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := Equiv.antisymm_iff

lemma Equiv.le : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 := by exact?

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := Eq.trans

lemma Equiv.antisymm_iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.antisymm_iff

alias ⟨_, Equiv.antisymm⟩ := by exact?

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

go (binders : Array (TSyntax ``extBinderParenthesized)) : Matcher := fun s => do
    -- `lit` is bound to the SubExpr that the `scoped` syntax produced
    s.withVar lit do
    try
      -- Run `smatcher` at `lit`, clearing the `scopeId` variable so that it can get a fresh value
      let s ← smatcher {s with vars := s.vars.erase scopeId}
      s.withVar scopeId do
        guard (← getExpr).isLambda
        let prop ← try Meta.isProp (← getExpr).bindingDomain! catch _ => pure false
        let isDep := (← getExpr).bindingBody!.hasLooseBVar 0
        let ppTypes ← getPPOption getPPPiBinderTypes -- the same option controlling ∀
        let dom ← withBindingDomain delab
        withBindingBodyUnusedName fun x => do
          let x : Ident := ⟨x⟩
          let binder ←
            if prop && !isDep then
              -- this underscore is used to support binder predicates, since it indicates
              -- the variable is unused and this binder is safe to merge into another
              `(extBinderParenthesized|(_ : $dom))
            else if prop || ppTypes then
              `(extBinderParenthesized|($x:ident : $dom))
            else
              `(extBinderParenthesized|($x:ident))
          -- Now use the body of the lambda for `lit` for the next iteration
          let s ← s.captureSubexpr lit
          -- TODO merge binders as an inverse to `satisfies_binder_pred%`
          let binders := binders.push binder
          go binders s
    catch _ =>
      guard <| !binders.isEmpty
      if let some binders₂ := s.scopeState then
        guard <| binders == binders₂ -- TODO: this might be a bit too strict, but it seems to work
        return s
      else
        return {s with scopeState := binders}

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := rfl

@[symm] lemma Equiv.symm : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓢 := Eq.symm

@[trans] lemma Equiv.trans : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 =ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓤 := by exact?

/--
Equality is transitive: if `a = b` and `b = c` then `a = c`.

Because this is in the `Eq` namespace, if you have variables or expressions
`h₁ : a = b` and `h₂ : b = c`, you can use `h₁.trans h₂ : a = c` as shorthand
for `Eq.trans h₁ h₂`.

For more information: [Equality](https://lean-lang.org/theorem_proving_in_lean4/quantifiers_and_equality.html#equality)
-/
theorem Eq.trans {α : Sort u} {a b c : α} (h₁ : Eq a b) (h₂ : Eq b c) : Eq a c :=
  h₂ ▸ h₁

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

/--
Equality is symmetric: if `a = b` then `b = a`.

Because this is in the `Eq` namespace, if you have a variable `h : a = b`,
`h.symm` can be used as shorthand for `Eq.symm h` as a proof of `b = a`.

For more information: [Equality](https://lean-lang.org/theorem_proving_in_lean4/quantifiers_and_equality.html#equality)
-/
@[symm] theorem Eq.symm {α : Sort u} {a b : α} (h : Eq a b) : Eq b a :=
  h ▸ rfl

informal_statement: The notion of inconsistency is preserved under equivalence in the context of logic systems. Specifically, any two theories that are not equivalent under a given equivalence relation are considered inconsistent with respect to each other.
informal_proof: Consider any two arbitrary theories, denoted as λ and μ, within the framework of logic. The definition of inconsistency in this context is grounded in the relationship between these theories. When λ and μ are not equivalent, meaning there is no equivalence established between them under the defined conditions, they fall outside the realm of theoretical equivalence. By the principle `inconsistent_iff_theory_eq`, which establishes a bidirectional relationship between inconsistency and theoretical equivalence, it follows that these two theories are inconsistent with respect to each other. This principle holds universally, as λ and μ were chosen arbitrarily from the set of all theories. Therefore, for any pair of theories, if they are not equivalent, they are deemed inconsistent. Thus, inconsistency is a property that retains its essence across different theories, maintaining its recognition as the absence of equivalence.

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by simp [Equiv, Set.ext_iff, theory]

@[simp, refl] protected lemma Equiv.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓢 := by exact?

C1_dependencies.content:
/--
`rfl : a = a` is the unique constructor of the equality type. This is the
same as `Eq.refl` except that it takes `a` implicitly instead of explicitly.

This is a more powerful theorem than it may appear at first, because although
the statement of the theorem is `a = a`, Lean will allow anything that is
definitionally equal to that type. So, for instance, `2 + 2 = 4` is proven in
Lean by `rfl`, because both sides are the same up to definitional equality.
-/
@[match_pattern] def rfl {α : Sort u} {a : α} : Eq a a := Eq.refl a

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  rintro ⟨h₁, nh₁⟩ ⟨h₂, _⟩;
  constructor;
  . exact WeakerThan.trans h₁ h₂;
  . apply not_weakerThan_iff.mpr;
    obtain ⟨f, hf₁, hf₂⟩ := not_weakerThan_iff.mp nh₁;
    use f;
    constructor;
    . apply weakerThan_iff.mp h₂;
      assumption;
    . assumption;

lemma weakening (h : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣) {f} : 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f := weakerThan_iff.mp h

lemma Equiv.iff : 𝓢 =ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ↔ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by exact?

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

@[trans]
lemma strictlyWeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 <ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓤 := by
  exact?

informal_statement: An inconsistent logical theory is equivalent to the theory of the universal type. Conversely, if a theory is equivalent to the universal type, then it is inconsistent.
informal_proof:
To establish this equivalence, we consider two directions.

First, suppose a theory is inconsistent. By definition, this means that within the theory, every formula can be derived, including all possible formulas. Therefore, the theory contains every formula, which aligns with it being equivalent to the universal type that includes all formulas.

Conversely, if a theory is equivalent to the universal type, it contains all possible formulas. Since the universal type is known to be inconsistent (as it allows the derivation of any formula), the theory must also be inconsistent to maintain this equivalence.

Hence, a theory is inconsistent if and only if it is equivalent to the theory of the universal type.

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

section

variable {𝓢 : S} {𝓣 : T} {𝓤 : U}

@[simp, refl] protected lemma WeakerThan.refl (𝓢 : S) : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓢 := Set.Subset.refl _

@[trans] lemma WeakerThan.trans : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 → 𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓤 → 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓤 := Set.Subset.trans

lemma weakerThan_iff : 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) :=
  ⟨fun h _ hf ↦ h hf, fun h _ hf ↦ h hf⟩

lemma not_weakerThan_iff : ¬𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊢! f ∧ 𝓣 ⊬ f) := by simp [weakerThan_iff, Unprovable];

lemma strictlyWeakerThan_iff : 𝓢 <ₛ 𝓣 ↔ (∀ {f}, 𝓢 ⊢! f → 𝓣 ⊢! f) ∧ (∃ f, 𝓢 ⊬ f ∧ 𝓣 ⊢! f) := by
  simp [StrictlyWeakerThan, weakerThan_iff]; intro _
  exact exists_congr (fun _ ↦ by simp [and_comm])

theorem sUnion_mem_empty_univ {S : Set (Set α)} (h : S ⊆ {∅, univ}) :
    ⋃₀ S ∈ ({∅, univ} : Set (Set α)) := by
  simp only [mem_insert_iff, mem_singleton_iff, or_iff_not_imp_left, sUnion_eq_empty, not_forall]
  rintro ⟨s, hs, hne⟩
  obtain rfl : s = univ := (h hs).resolve_left hne
  exact univ_subset_iff.1 <| subset_sUnion_of_mem hs

informal_proof:
To understand this theorem, let's first clarify the key concepts:

1. **Inconsistent Theory**: A formal theory is inconsistent if it contains a statement and its negation, meaning the theory can derive contradictory statements.
2. **Theory**: The set of all statements derivable within a formal system or framework.
3. **Set.univ**: The collection of all possible elements of a particular type.

The theorem states that a theory is inconsistent precisely when it encompasses every possible type, which is represented by `Set.univ`. To unpack this equivalence:

- **From Inconsistency to Theory Equaling the Universe**: If a theory is inconsistent, by definition, it can derive any statement. This includes all possible types, effectively making the theory equal to `Set.univ`. Conversely, if a theory equals `Set.univ`, it contains every possible type and thus can derive any statement, including contradictions, making it inconsistent.

- **Logical Equivalence**: The equivalence (`↔`) asserts that both directions hold:
  - If the theory is inconsistent (`Inconsistent ��`), then its theory equals `Set.univ`.
  - If the theory equals `Set.univ`, then the theory is inconsistent.

This completes the informal proof of the statement.

* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.

informal_statement: If a statement \( f \) is not provable in a formal system \( \mathcal{S} \), then \( \mathcal{S} \) is consistent.
informal_proof:
To establish that the formal system \( \mathcal{S} \) is consistent under the condition that there exists a statement \( f \) not provable in \( \mathcal{S} \), we proceed as follows:

1. **Assumption of Unprovability**: We begin by assuming that \( f \) is not provable in \( \mathcal{S} \).

2. **Suppose for Contradiction that \( \mathcal{S} \) is Inconsistent**: For the sake of argument, suppose that \( \mathcal{S} \) is inconsistent. By definition, an inconsistent system allows the derivation of any statement from its axioms.

3. **Derivation of \( f \) by Inconsistency**: Given the inconsistency of \( \mathcal{S} \), it would follow that \( f \) is provable in \( \mathcal{S} \), since every statement can be derived in an inconsistent system.

4. **Contradiction Arises**: This conclusion that \( f \) is provable directly contradicts our initial assumption that \( f \) is not provable.

5. **Conclusion of Consistency**: Since the assumption of \( \mathcal{S} \)'s inconsistency leads to a contradiction, we conclude that \( \mathcal{S} \) must be consistent.

Therefore, the existence of an unprovable statement \( f \) in a formal system \( \mathcal{S} \) necessitates that \( \mathcal{S} \) is consistent. This reasoning aligns with standard logical principles governing the consistency of formal systems.

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

informal_statement: For every natural number \( n \), there exists a prime number \( p \) such that \( p \) is greater than \( n \). Equivalently, there are infinitely many prime numbers.
informal_proof:
First, we fix an arbitrary natural number \( n \). 
Our goal is to show that there exists a prime number \( p \) greater than \( n \). 

Consider the number \( (n + 1)! + 1 \), where \( ! \) denotes the factorial function. 
Since \( n \) is a natural number, \( n + 1 \) is at least 2, making \( (n + 1)! \) at least 2. 
Therefore, \( (n + 1)! + 1 \) is at least 3, ensuring that it is greater than 1. 

By the fundamental theorem of arithmetic, every integer greater than 1 has at least one prime factor. 
Let \( p \) be a prime factor of \( (n + 1)! + 1 \). 
We aim to show that \( p \) is greater than \( n \). 

Assume, for the sake of contradiction, that \( p \) is not greater than \( n \). 
Since \( p \) is a prime factor of \( (n + 1)! + 1 \) and \( p \leq n \), \( p \) must divide \( (n + 1)! \) because the factorial includes all integers from 1 to \( n + 1 \). 
Therefore, \( p \) divides both \( (n + 1)! \) and \( (n + 1)! + 1 \). 
This implies that \( p \) divides their difference:
\[
(n + 1)! + 1 - (n + 1)! = 1
\]
Since \( p \) divides 1 and \( p \) is a prime number, this leads to a contradiction because all primes are greater than 1. 

Hence, our initial assumption that \( p \leq n \) must be false. 
Therefore, \( p > n \), and since \( p \) is a prime factor of \( (n + 1)! + 1 \), it follows that there exists a prime number greater than \( n \). 

This completes the proof that there are infinitely many prime numbers.

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv
annotation: infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

namespace LO

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

namespace System

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

def Provable (f : F) : Prop := Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢ f)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))

def WeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 ⊆ theory 𝓣

infix:40 " ≤ₛ " => WeakerThan

def StrictlyWeakerThan (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := 𝓢 ≤ₛ 𝓣 ∧ ¬𝓣 ≤ₛ 𝓢

infix:40 " <ₛ " => StrictlyWeakerThan

def Equiv (𝓢 : S) (𝓣 : T) : Prop := theory 𝓢 = theory 𝓣

infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv
annotation: infix:40 " =ₛ " => Equiv

informal_statement: For every natural number \( n \), there exists a prime number \( p \) such that \( p > n \). This demonstrates that there are infinitely many prime numbers.
informal_proof:
First, fix an arbitrary natural number \( n \). Consider the number \( m = (n + 1)! + 1 \), where \( (n + 1)! \) denotes the factorial of \( n + 1 \). By the definition of factorial, \( (n + 1)! \) is the product of all positive integers from 1 up to \( n + 1 \). Therefore, \( (n + 1)! \) is at least 1 and is a natural number. Adding 1 to \( (n + 1)! \) gives us a number \( m \) that is at least 2.

Since \( m \) is a natural number greater than 1, it must have at least one prime factor \( p \). These prime factors are greater than or equal to 2 and less than or equal to \( m \) itself. By the nature of the factorial, \( p \) cannot divide \( (n + 1)! \) because it would imply \( p \) is one of the factors in the product \( (n + 1)! \), and hence would divide \( m = (n + 1)! + 1 \) as well. However, such a \( p \) would divide both \( m \) and \( (n + 1)! \), and consequently would divide their difference:
\[
m - (n + 1)! = 1
\]
This implies that \( p \) divides 1, which is impossible since \( p \ge 2 \). Therefore, no such prime factor \( p \) can be less than or equal to \( n + 1 \).

Thus, the prime factor \( p \) of \( m \) must satisfy \( p > n + 1 \), ensuring \( p > n \). Since \( n \) was arbitrary, this holds for all natural numbers \( n \). Therefore, there is no finite bound on the size of prime numbers, proving that there are infinitely many primes.

import Foundation.Logic.LogicSymbol
import Foundation.Logic.Semantics
import Foundation.Vorspiel.Collection

/-!
# Basic definitions and properties of proof system related notions

This file defines a characterization of the system/proof/provability/calculus of formulae.
Also defines soundness and completeness.

## Main Definitions
* `LO.System F S`: a general framework of deductive system `S` for formulae `F`.
* `LO.System.Inconsistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that all formulae in `F` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `LO.System.Consistent 𝓢`: a proposition that states that `𝓢` is not inconsistent.
* `LO.System.Sound 𝓢 𝓜`: provability from `𝓢` implies satisfiability on `𝓜`.
* `LO.System.Complete 𝓢 𝓜`: satisfiability on `𝓜` implies provability from `𝓢`.

## Notation
* `𝓢 ⊢ φ`: a type of formalized proofs of `φ : F` from deductive system `𝓢 : S`.
* `𝓢 ⊢! φ`: a proposition that states there is a proof of `φ` from `𝓢`, i.e. `φ` is provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊬ φ`: a proposition that states `φ` is not provable from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢* T`: a type of formalized proofs for each formulae in a set `T` from `𝓢`.
* `𝓢 ⊢!* T`: a proposition that states each formulae in `T` is provable from `𝓢`.

-/

class System (F : outParam Type*) (S : Type*) where
  Prf : S → F → Type*

infix:45 " ⊢ " => System.Prf

variable {F : Type*} {S T U : Type*} [System F S] [System F T] [System F U]

section

variable (𝓢 : S)

abbrev Unprovable (f : F) : Prop := ¬Provable 𝓢 f

infix:45 " ⊢! " => Provable

infix:45 " ⊬ " => Unprovable

def PrfSet (s : Set F) : Type _ := {f : F} → f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢ f

def ProvableSet (s : Set F) : Prop := ∀ {f}, f ∈ s → 𝓢 ⊢! f

infix:45 " ⊢* " => PrfSet

infix:45 " ⊢!* " => ProvableSet

def theory : Set F := {f | 𝓢 ⊢! f}

end

lemma unprovable_iff_isEmpty {𝓢 : S} {f : F} :
    𝓢 ⊬ f ↔ IsEmpty (𝓢 ⊢ f) := by simp [Provable, Unprovable]

noncomputable def Provable.get {𝓢 : S} {f : F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢! f) : 𝓢 ⊢ f :=
  Classical.choice h

lemma provableSet_iff {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} :
    𝓢 ⊢!* s ↔ Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s) := by
  simp [ProvableSet, PrfSet, Provable, Classical.nonempty_pi, ←imp_iff_not_or]

noncomputable def ProvableSet.get {𝓢 : S} {s : Set F} (h : 𝓢 ⊢!* s) : 𝓢 ⊢* s :=
  Classical.choice (α := 𝓢 ⊢* s) (provableSet_iff.mp h : Nonempty (𝓢 ⊢* s))
